text.arabic_uthmani: نِّعْمَةًۭ مِّنْ عِندِنَا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى مَن شَكَرَ

words.gloss_range: an accusative indefinite favor/blessing naming the prior rescue as a sourced act of benefaction
words.root_gloss_range: favor, pleasant well-being, and ease are locally relevant; praise-formula, affirmation, livestock, ostrich, wind, walking, and other distant branches are not active here

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: source preposition following the favor noun

words.prose: {{ar:نِّعْمَةً}} ({{tr:niʿmatan}}) opens the ayah as an accusative continuation, so the reader must carry the rescue of 54:34 into the first word of 54:35. The word does not merely say that escape happened; it classifies that escape as one indefinite, exemplary favor, immediately qualified by source and able to become the case from which the later recompense rule generalizes. Its root field lets the favor feel like bestowed ease, while the local noun form keeps the active sense at a discrete gift rather than every branch of the root. The opening also starts a favor-gratitude-recompense circuit, with the first word answered by the final gratitude verb, touched by familiar favor-memory language, and joined to its source by the nasal movement into {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}).

topics.headline: accusative opening carries the prior rescue across the ayah boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins mid-syntax: the favor-word is grammatically tied back to the rescue in 54:34.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar marks an indefinite accusative functioning as state or specification, and the attachment evidence leaves no new local verb before the source phrase.

topics.headline: adjacent source phrase first qualifies the favor noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the favor receive its source before the ayah moves on to the reward clause.
topics.reason: The governed phrase {{ar:مِنْ عِندِنَا}} ({{tr:min ʿindinā}}) is syntactically adjacent to the opening noun and is treated as its source complement.

topics.headline: case compresses state, specification, and purpose-like force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one accusative noun carry several compatible ways of interpreting the rescue as favor.
topics.reason: The bundle licenses state or specification most directly; purpose and cognate-force language can survive as interpretive pressure, not as a single forced parse.

topics.headline: indefinite singular makes the rescue one example of favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is one favor from a larger divine field, not an exhausted total of blessing.
topics.reason: The noun is singular, indefinite, and marked with tanwīn; recurrence evidence compares this isolated instance with wider uncountable-favor language (14:34).

topics.headline: favor branch carries ease without importing distant branches
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the rescue as divinely given ease, not bare survival.
topics.reason: V4 supports pleasant well-being, bestowed favor, and softness/ease as local branches, while unrelated branches such as affirmation, livestock, ostrich imagery, and walking are blocked by the abstract noun context.

topics.headline: opening favor is answered by closing gratitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah framed by gift at the start and grateful response at the end.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows identify the favor-gratitude-recompense circuit, and the word order places this noun before the later recompense and gratitude words.

topics.headline: favor-memory recurrence is backgrounded into this local rescue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear familiar favor-memory language, while the local referent remains the protected family event.
topics.reason: The row gives a real recurrence field but no concrete citation, so the prose keeps it as local background rather than a specific inter-ayah claim.

topics.headline: nasal cadence binds favor to source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the favor-word leaning into its source phrase instead of standing alone.
topics.reason: The rows describe the local recitation and sound contact between the tanwīn ending and the following source preposition.

topics.headline: escape is reread as sourced favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the predawn rescue reclassified from event into divine benefaction.
topics.reason: Boundary rows tie the saved family and the prior scene of 54:34 to the opening noun of 54:35.

words.gloss_range: source preposition; partitive pressure is possible as a secondary nuance under the source reading

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: favor noun qualified by the source phrase

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) turns the favor into something traced from a source, not simply a label placed after the rescue. Its strongest local job is to govern {{ar:عِندِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}) as the origin of {{ar:نِّعْمَةً}} ({{tr:niʿmatan}}); the partitive idea may add the sense of one portion from a divine reserve, but it remains subordinate to source grammar. The nasal contact with the preceding tanwīn makes the source phrase sound attached to the blessing it qualifies.

topics.headline: source preposition makes origin grammatical
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine sourcehood is grammatically staged by a preposition, not left as an inference.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces {{ar:عِندِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}) as the governed complement of {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}); partitive force survives only as a secondary nuance because source is the local syntactic relation.

topics.headline: nasal contact fuses blessing and source marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the source marker cling to the favor-word at the phrase boundary.
topics.reason: The rows point to the recitational contact between the tanwīn of {{ar:نِّعْمَةً}} ({{tr:niʿmatan}}) and the following mīm of {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}).

words.gloss_range: from Our presence/domain; locative possession and source are locally active
words.root_gloss_range: proximity, presence, and possession-domain are active; obstinate resistance and sideward-flow branches are only contrastive background and not local sense

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: reward verb later in the policy clause
generic recipient pronoun in the reward clause

words.prose: {{ar:عِندِنَا}} ({{tr:ʿindinā}}) lands the opening beat at a divine source-domain: the favor is from Our presence, with the first-person plural suffix fused to the locative itself. The root evidence can make that nearness feel firm and possessed, but the local adverbial form blocks importing the root family’s obstinate-resistance branch as the sense of the word. Compared with other proximity wording, this choice foregrounds domain and possession, and the nasal thread carries the phrase onward toward {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) and {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}).

topics.headline: locative plus suffix makes the source a divine domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the blessing comes from a possessed divine domain, not an unspecified origin.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word the governed complement of {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), and morphology gives it the first-person plural possessive suffix.

topics.headline: root tension yields firm proximity, not obstinacy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader gets stable divine nearness without misreading the word as stubbornness or resistance.
topics.reason: V4 lists proximity/presence as the active local branch for this adverbial form; resistance and deviation branches are real root background but not the selected local sense.

topics.headline: chosen proximity wording joins the reward-gratitude network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the source phrase as part of the ayah’s reward logic, not a detachable devotional aside.
topics.reason: The rows contrast this proximity/domain word with alternatives and connect it distributionally with reward and gratitude fields; concrete comparison references include 11:58 and 15:56.

topics.headline: nasal continuity connects source, action, and recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears source, reward action, and recipient class carried by a connected nasal movement.
topics.reason: The rows identify local sound continuity from the source phrase into the following reward clause.

words.gloss_range: comparison/manner particle fused into the compound thus/in that way

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: reward verb framed by the manner phrase

words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) begins the compact hinge {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:kadhālika}}). It keeps comparison and manner together: the previous rescue becomes the model, and the following clause states that recompense happens in that way. Because the pivot arrives without a conjunction after {{ar:مِنْ عِندِنَا}} ({{tr:min ʿindinā}}), the ayah shifts cleanly from sourced favor to principle rather than adding another loose modifier, and its open-vowel cadence resets the ear before {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}).

topics.headline: comparison particle scopes over the reward clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the rescue turned into a model for how divine recompense works.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:kadhālika}}) as a manner phrase modifying {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}), while the CRITICAL rows preserve the comparison force inside that manner use.

topics.headline: absence of conjunction sharpens the turn to principle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the second beat resume as principle rather than continue as a coordinated source phrase.
topics.reason: The local sequence moves from {{ar:مِنْ عِندِنَا}} ({{tr:min ʿindinā}}) directly into {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:kadhālika}}) without a coordinating particle.

topics.headline: open-vowel cadence resets before the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a reset before the reward verb enters.
topics.reason: The row identifies the local sound shape of the compound before {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}).

words.gloss_range: distal demonstrative within the compound, pointing to the prior rescue as the pattern for the reward clause
words.prose: {{ar:ذَٰلِكَ}} ({{tr:dhālika}}) packages the prior rescue as one pointable case before {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) arrives. Its hinge position lets the pointer face backward to the narrated rescue and forward to the policy clause, so event and rule define each other. In the compound {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:kadhālika najzī}}), the demonstrative also participates in a recognizable reward-closure formula, with concrete parallels such as 37:80, 37:105, 37:110, 37:121, 37:131, and 77:44.

topics.headline: distal demonstrative turns the rescue into a pointable case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior scene abstracted into a case record for recompense.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence says the demonstrative points back to the rescue event; the masculine singular surface can package a discourse event as one identifiable case.

topics.headline: demonstrative binds backward event and forward rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word does not only refer backward; it also opens the rule that follows.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows preserve the two-way deictic effect, and attachment evidence places the compound as a manner frame for the verb that follows.

topics.headline: compound participates in recurrent reward closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the local Lot rescue sealed with a broader Quranic reward formula.
topics.reason: Rows identify the recurring {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:kadhālika najzī}}) pattern and give concrete parallels: 37:80, 37:105, 37:110, 37:121, 37:131, and 77:44.

words.gloss_range: We recompense/reward; positive here because the object is the grateful one, with reward substance compressed by the prior favor
words.root_gloss_range: recompense, requital, reward, punishment, settlement, and sufficiency belong to the root range; the local clause selects active divine recompense, not tax, debt collection, or mere sufficing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: direct object and generic recipient of the reward verb

words.prose: {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) is the ayah’s active policy verb. Its object is {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), while the reward substance is compressed by the earlier favor, so the verb joins source, gift, recipient, and gratitude into one relation. The imperfect first-person plural form turns the completed rescue of 54:34 into an ongoing divine practice, with agency carried inside the verb rather than by a separate named subject. The root can cover reward and punishment, but here the grateful object makes it positive; the same root at 54:14 marks the opposite pole. In the formula {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:kadhālika najzī}}), the verb supplies the recurring action that makes the pointed-to rescue a general recompense pattern, while the near-sound handoff from rescue language to recompense language makes that shift audible.

topics.headline: verb joins implicit reward substance to explicit grateful recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the reward verb as the hub connecting prior favor, divine source, and grateful recipient.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) the direct object of the verb, while CRITICAL rows connect the reward substance back to the favor named earlier.

topics.headline: imperfect first-person plural states ongoing divine policy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from a completed rescue to a standing divine practice.
topics.reason: QAC and verb-instance evidence mark an imperfect 1cp active verb with implicit divine subject agreement, contrasting with the prior completed narrative rescue.

topics.headline: bidirectional recompense root is positive in this object frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a single recompense mechanism whose local outcome is reward because the recipient is grateful.
topics.reason: V4 supports recompense/requital as the relevant root branch and also records settlement-related branches; the local object {{ar:مَنْ شَكَرَ}} ({{tr:man shakara}}) narrows the polarity to reward, while 54:14 supplies a same-surah punitive contrast.

topics.headline: reward formula converts narrative into general rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the Lot episode closed as one instance of a recurring reward formula.
topics.reason: Rows identify the recurring {{ar:كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:kadhālika najzī}}) pattern with concrete parallels including 37:80, 37:105, 37:110, 37:121, 37:131, and 77:44.

topics.headline: near-sound handoff moves from rescue to recompense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the clause pivot from rescue language into recompense language.
topics.reason: The rows identify the local sound relation between the prior rescue root and the reward verb, plus the nasal-zay turn that centers the policy clause.

words.gloss_range: the one who/whoever; generic relative object of the reward verb and subject of the following gratitude verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: reward verb governing the relative pronoun
gratitude verb defining the recipient class

words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens the recipient class. It is the object of {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}), but it receives definition only through {{ar:شَكَرَ}} ({{tr:shakara}}), so the rewarded party is not lineage, era, or named rescue-group but whoever fulfills gratitude. Its fixed surface can support both relative and conditional force, and its position makes it the hinge between recompense and the gratitude condition; its nasal sound also bridges the reward verb to the final response.

topics.headline: unrestricted relative creates an open beneficiary class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from Lot’s rescued family to an open class defined by gratitude.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats {{ar:مَنْ شَكَرَ}} ({{tr:man shakara}}) as the object expression of the reward verb and as a generic relative referent.

topics.headline: same surface lets relative and whoever force work together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear both the one who and whoever, strengthening the maxim-like reach of the clause.
topics.reason: The surface form is indeclinable and compatible with relative or conditional force in the CRITICAL rows; attachment evidence preserves generic reference rather than a named antecedent.

topics.headline: fixed form carries object role into the gratitude clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one small word turn the reward verb’s object into the subject of the qualifying act.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) as direct object of {{ar:نَجْزِى}} ({{tr:najzī}}) and subject of {{ar:شَكَرَ}} ({{tr:shakara}}).

topics.headline: nasal sound bridges verb and condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the small pronoun join recompense to gratitude.
topics.reason: The row identifies the local nasal bridge between the reward verb and the final gratitude verb.

words.gloss_range: was grateful, acknowledged benefit; no explicit object is expressed, so the act is broad while context recalls the favor
words.root_gloss_range: recognizing and displaying favor is local; thriving-on-little and productive-yield imagery can color the response, while unrelated turbulence, euphemistic, and tribal-name branches are not active

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: generic relative subject of the gratitude verb

words.prose: {{ar:شَكَرَ}} ({{tr:shakara}}) closes the ayah on the human qualifying response. The verb has no explicit object, so the earlier favor remains recoverable without narrowing the rule to only one thanked item. Its perfect Form I makes gratitude a fulfilled act attached to the generic {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), broad in threshold but complete enough to qualify for recompense. Semantically, gratitude is acknowledgment and making benefit known, the positive answer to denial; 54:14 supplies the same-surah opposite pole. The productive root image can color gratitude as visible response to provision, while the local branch remains grateful acknowledgment rather than every derivative sense. As the final word, it answers the opening favor and makes the maxim read: the rewarded class is whoever has truly responded with gratitude.

topics.headline: omitted object keeps gratitude broad while context recalls favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that gratitude is not limited by a stated object, even though the opening favor remains in view.
topics.reason: Verb-instance evidence marks no explicit object for {{ar:شَكَرَ}} ({{tr:shakara}}), and translation support warns that target languages may be tempted to supply one.

topics.headline: perfect Form I presents fulfilled gratitude as criterion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees gratitude as a completed qualifying act, not merely an ongoing mood or intensified specialty form.
topics.reason: QAC marks a Form I perfect 3ms verb; attachment evidence links its hidden subject to generic {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}).

topics.headline: gratitude names acknowledgment against denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the saved side defined by acknowledgment rather than denial or concealment.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL semantic rows define gratitude as acknowledgment/display of benefit and contrast it with the same-surah denial field at 54:14.

topics.headline: root image makes gratitude visible response to provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses gratitude as benefit made visible in response, not only private feeling.
topics.reason: V4 supports the primary branch of recognizing/displaying favor and separate productive-yield branches; those images can color the local act, while divine-appreciation references such as 35:30 and 42:23 remain broader root background rather than the local subject.

topics.headline: beneficiary becomes active responder in reward relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the recipient of recompense as an active responder whose gratitude grounds the reward relation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the same {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) the object of reward and subject of gratitude; inter-ayah rows connect gratitude with added divine response at 14:7.

topics.headline: final word supplies the maxim’s condition and answers the opening favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah end on the criterion by which the whole rescue and reward statement is read.
topics.reason: Word order places {{ar:شَكَرَ}} ({{tr:shakara}}) as the final word, after the generic relative and reward verb, and rows explicitly pair it with the opening favor.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: نِّعْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا ... نَجْزِى مَن شَكَرَ
baseline_models.mechanism: A benefaction is marked by its source, recognized by its recipient, and answered by fitting recompense; provenance, reception, and return form one reciprocal circuit.

activation_trace.role: Benefaction and improved condition supply the good that enters the reciprocal circuit.
Near presence fixes the benefaction's provenance rather than leaving it an anonymous good.
Act-for-act recompense makes the second clause answer the first.
Recognition and manifested praise supply the recipient response that closes the circuit.

changed_reading.before: A favor is given, followed by a general maxim that grateful people are rewarded.
changed_reading.after: The ayah presents provenance-aware reciprocity: a benefit from the divine presence is recognized by its recipient and answered with fitting recompense.

baseline_models.mechanism: The increase branch of benefaction and the small-input, visible-effect branch of gratitude make gratefulness a high-gain response: received good becomes productive in the receiver and invites renewed increase.

activation_trace.role: Increase and intensification give the initial benefaction an expandable vector.
A little input producing a visible effect models gratitude as responsive uptake rather than mere speech.
Recompense returns increase to the recipient's productive response.

changed_reading.before: Gratitude is verbal thanks for an already completed gift.
changed_reading.after: Gratitude is receptivity that makes even a small gift visibly productive, while recompense renews the increase rather than adding a detached prize.

baseline_models.mechanism: The substitution branch of recompense allows the sourced benefaction itself to stand in for and suffice on behalf of the grateful recipient; gift and reward need not be separate objects.

activation_trace.role: The benefaction supplies the concrete good that can itself function as recompense.
Standing in for another and sufficing makes recompense protective substitution rather than only added payment.
Recognition identifies the recipient for whom the sourced good suffices.

changed_reading.before: Reward is an extra item delivered after gratitude.
changed_reading.after: The favor can itself be the recompense: a provision from the giver that stands in for, covers, and suffices for the grateful person.

context_deltas.mechanism: Warnings and manifest signs invite recognition; denial contradicts them and kufr can cover a benefaction. This makes شكر the active opposite: receiving, acknowledging, and showing the sourced favor, with recompense following that disclosed stance.

activation_trace.role: The benefaction is the object that can either be recognized and shown or covered.
Recognition and manifestation define the positive response to the disclosed good.
Contradiction of truth supplies the first negative mirror of grateful recognition.
Warning that awakens caution supplies content meant to be received rather than disputed.
The manifest sign makes recognition an evidential response, not only an affective one.
Covering a benefaction directly reverses the focus branch's recognition and manifestation.

structural_cues: Denial recurs around warnings and all the signs, while 54:35 uses the inferential كَذَٰلِكَ and the generalizing مَن.
The later label كُفَّارُ supplies a branch-level polarity with the focus pair نِعْمَةً and شَكَرَ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies warnings, manifest signs, denial, and the covering-of-benefaction branch; I infer that recognition versus concealment is the response axis carried into كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِى. A live alternative is that شكر remains ordinary thanks after rescue and the epistemic polarity is only contextual.

changed_reading.before: Whoever feels or voices thanks receives a reward.
changed_reading.after: Whoever refuses to cover what has been disclosed, recognizes its source, and lets the benefaction become manifest is met with the corresponding recompense.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context moves from a named people to a collective boast of gathered victory and then to a broken line turning its back. Against that sequence, مَن شَكَرَ states a portable response criterion that group identity and cohesion cannot replace.

activation_trace.role: Recognition supplies the qualifying response attached to the unrestricted مَن.
Recompense follows the response criterion rather than collective standing.
A people as a social collective supplies the identity scale that the focus criterion cuts across.
Gathering dispersed members into one body supplies the claimed mechanism of collective security.
Aid and manifested victory state what the gathered group expects from itself.
Breaking and driving back a battle line reverses the group's claimed cohesion.
Turning the back completes the reversal from self-declared victory to retreat.

structural_cues: The generic construction مَن شَكَرَ contrasts with the plural boast نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ.
54:45 immediately answers gathered victory with defeat and turned backs.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies collective labels, a group boast, and its military reversal; I infer that the singularly predicated response in مَن شَكَرَ is deliberately non-corporate. A live alternative is that مَن is merely generic grammar with no contrastive force.

changed_reading.before: The maxim promises reward without specifying how it relates to social identity.
changed_reading.after: Recompense tracks anyone's enacted recognition, while inherited peoplehood, numerical cohesion, and claimed mutual victory provide no substitute criterion.

context_deltas.mechanism: A household is separated from a pelting destructive field. The focus benefaction therefore becomes an outcome-changing extraction, and the sufficiency branch of جزاء lets that rescue stand in place of the fate otherwise surrounding the recipients.

activation_trace.role: Benefaction names the good condition produced by removal from the destructive field.
Protective sufficiency allows the rescue itself to replace the threatened outcome as recompense.
A stone-driving wind supplies the encompassing destructive field from which removal matters.
The household as those who return to one another defines the social unit extracted.
Deliverance by separation supplies the spatial operation that turns favor into rescue.

structural_cues: The exception إِلَّآ ءَالَ لُوطٍ and نَجَّيْنَٰهُم immediately precede the accusative نِعْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a pelting agent, an excepted household, and deliverance by separation; I infer that نِعْمَةً names the selective extraction and that نجزي generalizes its logic. A live alternative is that نِعْمَةً is only a causal gloss on rescue without a substitution mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The favor is an unspecified positive gift.
changed_reading.after: The favor is a selective change of outcome: the grateful recipient is separated out, and rescue itself suffices as the recompense.

context_deltas.mechanism: Pre-dawn rescue and morning punishment occupy one temporal threshold but produce opposite settled outcomes. The focus maxim becomes the hinge naming a timed differentiation rather than an indefinitely deferred reward.

activation_trace.role: Fitting recompense links the two opposed outcomes at the shared temporal threshold.
The last part of night locates rescue just before the threshold turns.
Arrival in the morning supplies the matching time of the contrary outcome.
Early morning sharpens the temporal correspondence with pre-dawn rescue.
Fixity and settlement make the morning outcome durable rather than momentary.

structural_cues: 54:35 stands between rescue بِسَحَرٍ and punishment that arrives بُكْرَةً as مُسْتَقِرّ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies pre-dawn rescue, morning arrival, and settled punishment; I infer that their near-parallel timing makes 54:35 a threshold-sorting rule. A live alternative is that the times only mark narrative chronology and do not modify نجزي.

changed_reading.before: Recompense is a general future consequence with no temporal texture.

The storm-exception-rescue sequence recast favor as selective extraction and protective substitution.
Ease and reminder reframed gratitude as high-gain uptake in which a small accessible cue becomes visibly productive.

summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah's own branches form a provenance-reception-return circuit; the context then changes that circuit spatially, temporally, epistemically, socially, sensorially, and juridically without forcing the readings into one final interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The pre-dawn and morning parallel may be only narrative chronology rather than a semantic timing mechanism.
The guest-provenance model is a relational analogy whose directional link remains exploratory.
The ج ز ي to ج ز ز harvest model and other material-yield images must remain explicitly analogical.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Near-source favor is answered by recognition that shows effects.** `ن ع م` B001 is bestowed favor and pleasant well-being; `ع ن د` B004 is proximity/presence; `ج ز ي` B001 is matching recompense; `ش ك ر` B001 is recognizing a favor and praising its giver, while B002 is being sustained by little and showing its effect. The rescue is appositionally named a favor “from Our presence,” then generalized as recompense. I infer a reciprocal visibility: favor comes near, gratitude recognizes it, and recompense makes that recognition effective. The ayah reads gratitude as perceptive response with observable consequence.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 54:54–55 supplies the surah’s fullest positive recompense: gardens, river, a sound seat, and proximity `عِندَ` the sovereign. The repeated proximity root makes this local rescue a smaller instance of final nearness.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **`ن ع م / B001` (pleasant well-being and bestowed favor) with `B002` (softness and easeful living).** The favor is concretely the household's low-friction passage out before the pebble storm. The packet supplies timed rescue and names it favor; I infer protected transit -> is the material form of beneficence. **Reading change:** `نِعْمَة` is not an added gift after rescue; rescue itself is the bestowed ease.
2. **`ج ز ي / B001` (recompense matching an act) with `ش ك ر / B001` (recognizing a favor and praising the benefactor).** The general `كَذَلِكَ` turns the episode into a reciprocal rule: recognition is answered by preserving favor's recipient. The packet states recompense and gratitude; I infer recognized benefaction -> matched benefaction, while the exact form of matching is supplied by the rescue context. **Reading change:** gratitude is causal participation in a reciprocity, not verbal courtesy alone.
3. **`ع ن د / B004` (proximity and presence at something).** `مِنْ عِندِنَا` locates favor at a source of presence while the household is separated from its hostile social surroundings. The packet supplies removal from one proximity and favor from another; I infer changed nearness -> changed protection. **Reading change:** rescue relocates the household's operative relation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 54:36-39 sharpened recompense by contrast: disputed warning becomes settled punishment and tasting, while the fixed ayah identifies rescue itself as the matched favor for gratitude.

Birine karşı durup onunla boy ölçüşmek, kimi durumda onun yaptığının benzerini yaparak yarışmak anlamına gelir.

facets.statement: Bir varlık izlenen yoldan veya ortak doğrultudan yana sapar.
Bir kişi ya da deve topluluğa karışmayıp ayrı bir yanda durur.

Yolun eğik uzanması, saplama vuruşunun sağa sola gitmesi ve bir okun ötekilerden başka yönde çıkması bu ayrılmanın özel örnekleridir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Birleşen kanıt, ortak yol veya topluluktan yana ayrılma çekirdeğini; yan adı, ayrı duran insan ve deve, eğik yol ve başka yönde çıkan ok gibi somut gerçekleşmelerle gösterir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi aynı sözü kadın cinsel organı ve cinsel birleşme ya da evlilik için örtülü anlatım olarak kaydeder; çoğul biçim de kadınların cinsel organlarını gösterir. Geçici çerçeve bu örtmeceli kullanım alanını doğru sınırlar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Örtmece çekirdeği korunur; kadınla kurulan söz öbeği ve topluluk bildiren biçim kendi cinsel organ anlamlarıyla ayrı tutulur.
